follow100Note: Of the $9.79 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, about $0.87 belongs to noncontrolling partners — $8.93 is Disney shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $1,336M, Sports $652M, Experiences $2,615M (before corporate costs). Of the $2,465M of net income, $218M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $2,247M is attributable to Disney shareholders. The cost split (cost of services / cost of products) comes from Disney's Q2 FY26 10-Q; the earnings release reports the same totals.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $1.81 — last year had a one-off tax benefit

oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $239M in the quarter.

The year-ago quarter included a one-off income-tax benefit of about $1.0B from the resolution of a prior-year tax matter — the main reason reported EPS fell year over year despite higher profit before tax.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $240M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $57M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 7% to $25.2B. Entertainment revenue grew 10% — Avatar: Fire and Ash and Zootopia 2 in theaters, plus streaming subscribers paying higher rates — and Experiences (parks and cruises) grew 7%.
takeaways.title: Streaming and theaters carried growth

takeaways.text: Experiences operating income rose 5% to $2.6B — more than Entertainment ($1.3B) and Sports ($652M) combined — as guests kept spending at the parks.
takeaways.title: Parks are the profit engine

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS dropped from $1.81 to $1.27 even though pre-tax profit rose 9%: the year-ago quarter included a one-off ~$1.0B tax benefit from resolving a prior-year tax matter. Adjusted EPS, which strips out one-offs, rose 8% to $1.57.
takeaways.title: Reported EPS fell — blame last year

verdict: Disney's revenue rose 7% to $25.2B and adjusted EPS grew 8% — but reported EPS fell to $1.27 because last year's quarter was flattered by a one-off ~$1.0B tax benefit.
